schema.description: UHN Minimal Risk ICF Automation Pipeline — canonical template registry.

symbol_guide.{{placeholder}}: REQUIRED substitution. Replace the entire {{...}} token with study-specific information extracted from the protocol.
symbol_guide.{{option1/option2}}: CHOOSE ONE. Pick the applicable option from the slash-separated list inside the braces (e.g., {{will/may}}, {{you/they}}, {{study/clinical trial}}).
symbol_guide.<Condition label>: CONDITIONAL BLOCK (single angle brackets). Include the text that follows this marker only if the stated condition applies to the study. Typically used for a single-paragraph or single-sentence addition (e.g., <If applicable>, <For studies involving Focus Groups>).
symbol_guide.<<Condition block>>: CONDITIONAL BLOCK (double angle brackets). Same meaning as <...> but conventionally marks a larger or more distinct scenario block, often with mutually exclusive alternatives (e.g., <<If a fresh tissue sample is required>>, <<If data sent outside Canada>>). Treat identically to <...> for extraction purposes.
symbol_guide.OR (standalone line): ALTERNATIVE. Choose exactly one of the blocks immediately above or below this marker — do not include both.
symbol_guide.• or - (list markers): BULLET POINT. Both markers are used interchangeably as list items.

field_guide.heading: UPPERCASE section heading as it appears in the ICF template.
field_guide.sub_section: Sub-section name, or null if none. Use angle brackets (e.g. '<Focus Groups>') when the label is a conditional template block rather than a true heading in the source ICF template — the draft renderer shows these as bold grey italic.
field_guide.required: true = must be included; false = include only if relevant to this study.
field_guide.complexity: Classification tags indicating extraction difficulty and protocol availability. Drives the RLM iteration budget and availability flags.
field_guide.is_in_protocol: true if the information is expected to be findable in the study protocol.
field_guide.partially_in_protocol: true if only some fields can be extracted from the protocol; the rest require manual entry by the study team.
field_guide.is_standard_text: true if required_text is boilerplate that can be used verbatim — no extraction needed.
field_guide.instructions: Author-facing directions for writing this ICF section. Not participant-facing. Used to guide LLM extraction.
field_guide.required_text: Mandated ICF wording. Contains {{placeholders}} to be filled in. Empty string if the section uses suggested_text only.
field_guide.suggested_text: Sample ICF language to use as a starting point. Contains <conditions>, <<block conditions>>, {{placeholders}}, and OR alternatives. Not required wording — adapt to the study.
field_guide.suggested_text_format: 'text' (default) or 'html' — set to 'html' and use an HTML string in suggested_text when table content is needed.
field_guide.adaptation_notes: Runtime-only field. Set by the dynamic adaptation pass to inject study-specific context into extraction prompts. Always null in the base registry; never serialised back to this file.

schema.template_notes: This registry encodes the UHN Minimal Risk ICF Template (Document Version Date 22Oct2024). It differs from the standard (non-minimal) ICF template: there is no separate 'WHAT IS THE BACKGROUND INFORMATION FOR THIS STUDY?' section, no 'WHAT OTHER CHOICES ARE THERE?' section, no 'ASSIGNMENT TO A GROUP' section, no 'WHAT IS THE STUDY INTERVENTION?' section, no separate 'WHAT ARE THE STUDY PROCEDURES?' heading (procedures are described under 'WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?'), no 'WHAT ARE THE REPRODUCTIVE RISKS?' section, and no 'DATA SAFETY MONITORING' section. The risk section (18) only describes risks of study-related procedures (no separate intervention-risk subsection 18.1). Several sections that contain mandated text in the standard template (e.g., 16, 17, 21.1, 23, 26) are presented as suggested/example text in the minimal risk template.

sections.heading: Summary of Informed Consent Form
sections.required_text:
Below is a summary of information about the study.  There is more information in the document called an "informed consent form" that follows this summary.  Please read the informed consent form.   The research team will also talk to you about the study and you can ask any questions you may have.

Participation in research is voluntary.  It is your choice whether you take part in this study.

sections.heading: Summary of Informed Consent Form
sections.instructions: Provide a brief description of the primary reason why the research is being conducted, in no more than 2-3 sentences, written in plain language.
sections.required_text:
Study purpose
The purpose of this study is {{provide a brief description of the primary reason why the research is being conducted, no more than 2-3 sentences.}}

sections.heading: Summary of Informed Consent Form
sections.instructions: Provide the expected duration of study participation and the period of time participants will be followed.
sections.required_text: It is expected that study participation will last {{provide expected duration}}.  Participants will be followed for {{define period of time.}}

sections.heading: Summary of Informed Consent Form
sections.instructions:
Briefly describe and highlight key study procedures and, if applicable, outline procedures that may be lengthy/burdensome to participants

Fill the placeholders in the required text: name the interventional group(s); briefly describe the key procedures (e.g., the frequency of study visits and what happens at them); and, if applicable, describe any lengthy or burdensome procedures and how much extra time they take. The 'If applicable:' clause about lengthy/burdensome procedures should be included only when such procedures exist. You are allowed to edit the required text a bit at the end just to make the paragraph coherent and in plain grade 8 correct language
sections.required_text: This study is looking at {{describe interventional group(s).}}  Participants will also {{briefly describe key procedures}} study visits every {{X}} weeks during which the researchers will do some tests.  <Only include the following sentence if lengthy or burdensome procedures exist:> You will be asked to do {{describe lengthy or burdensome procedures}} which may take {{specify time}} extra time.

sections.heading: Summary of Informed Consent Form
sections.instructions:
Describe the most important risks. Consider those most probable and/or of highest magnitude of harm. This summary should NOT include the full list of risks.

For the 'most likely' risks: include the risks participants are most likely to experience, specified in lay language with their expected frequency. Provide one bullet per risk.

For the 'most serious' risks: include this part only if applicable. For the purposes of this summary, serious risks are considered those that may result in death, hospitalization, or are permanent. Specify each in lay language with expected frequency, one bullet per risk.

sections.heading: Summary of Informed Consent Form
sections.instructions: Insert the direct benefit, or state if there is no direct benefit. The suggested text holds a placeholder for the benefit statement, followed by a conditional example: if direct benefit to the participant is unknown but there is a greater benefit to society, include the example sentence ('We do not know if you will receive medical benefit...'); otherwise replace the placeholder with the study-specific direct-benefit statement and omit the example.
sections.suggested_text:
{{Insert direct benefit, or state if there is no direct benefit.}}
<If direct benefit to participant is unknown but there is a greater benefit to society, include for example:> We do not know if you will receive medical benefit from participation but researchers hope that this study will fulfil its purpose and benefit others in future.

sections.heading: Summary of Informed Consent Form
sections.instructions: State that the participant does not have to participate to receive medical care if applicable to this study (include the suggested text). If it's not applicable to this study (i.e. the study is not about receiving medical care), leave this section empty.
sections.suggested_text: You do not have to participate in this study to receive medical care.

sections.heading: Informed Consent Form for Participation in a Research Study
sections.instructions:
Insert the study title verbatim, exactly as written on the protocol. Do not modify, rephrase, shorten, or simplify the title in any way — the AI must never alter the protocol title.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Copy only the full title text itself. Do not prefix it with labels such as "Study Title:", "Full title:", "TITLE:", or any similar heading — those labels are already provided by the ICF template. Do not place anything else next to or after the full title (no parenthetical plain-language rewrite, no "Simplified study title", no invented lay title).

Only include a short title if the protocol itself provides one; if included, reproduce that short title verbatim as well on a separate line as "Short Title: <verbatim short title>". Do not invent, generate, or create a simplified/lay short title when the protocol does not contain one.

sections.heading: Informed Consent Form for Participation in a Research Study
sections.instructions: Insert sponsor’s study ID if applicable.
sections.suggested_text: {{Insert sponsor’s study ID if applicable}}

sections.instructions: Listing Co-Investigators is discouraged, but should be considered for studies involving expertise from different departments (e.g., multimodal studies).
sections.suggested_text: [Co-Investigators: {{list names, titles, and departments if applicable}}]

sections.heading: Informed Consent Form for Participation in a Research Study
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
Insert the name of the Sponsor or, if applicable, the funder(s) of the research as documented in the protocol and/or application form, including, if applicable, drug suppliers. In general, UHN should not be indicated as a sponsor unless the UHN is a regulatory sponsor, then the entity that funds the study should be indicated as well as non-for-profit status of the UHN.

Should communication via e-mail be suggested, when providing an e-mail address, include a disclaimer (as applicable). Only UHN email addresses should be provided to participants.
sections.suggested_text:
{{Insert the name of the Sponsor or, if applicable, the funder(s) of the research}}

<If email communication is suggested — choose ONE of the following>
Please note that communication via e-mail is not absolutely secure. Thus, please do not communicate personal sensitive information via e-mail.
OR
Please note that the security of e-mail messages is not guaranteed. Messages may be forged, forwarded, kept indefinitely, or seen by others using the Internet. Do not use e-mail to discuss information you think is sensitive. Do not use e-mail in an emergency since e-mail may be delayed.

sections.heading: INTRODUCTION
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
{{main features of population}}: Describe only the direct circumstance that makes the individual eligible for this study. Focus on the specific condition, diagnosis, treatment, procedure, or clinical situation that is relevant to study participation (e.g., 'you have been diagnosed with [condition]', 'you are scheduled for [procedure]', 'you are a healthy adult volunteer'). Do not explain the full eligibility criteria, demographic requirements (e.g., age ranges), symptoms, underlying disease details, or provide descriptions of medical procedures unless they are necessary to understand why the person is being approached for the study.

{{Specify other potential participant concerns}}: Specify any other areas where participants might be concerned about a potential penalty or discrimination (e.g., 'the decision will not affect your employment'). Omit if no such concerns apply.
sections.required_text:
You are being invited to participate in a research study. You are invited to participate in this study because you {{explain the main features of the population to which the research applies}}. This consent form provides you with information to help you make an informed choice. Please read this document carefully and ask any questions you may have.  All your questions should be answered to your satisfaction before you decide whether to participate in this research study.

Please take your time in making your decision.  You may find it helpful to discuss it with your friends and family.

Taking part in this study is voluntary.  You have the option to not participate at all or you may choose to leave the study at any time.  Whatever you choose, it will not affect the usual medical care that you receive outside the study. {{Specify any other potential areas where participants might be concerned about a potential penalty or discrimination, such as the decision will not affect your employment — omit if none apply}}.

sections.heading: IS THERE A CONFLICT OF INTEREST?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
ALWAYS include this section — every ICF must declare conflicts of interest (or state there are none).

Describe any conflict of interest that exists or may appear to exist as it relates to any of the investigators, study staff or member of their immediate family. A conflict of interest exists if there is a potential benefit to the investigator(s), study staff or member of their immediate family including the professional benefit from academic achievement or presentation of the results. Examples include, but are not limited to, speaker’s fees, travel assistance, consultant fees, honoraria, gifts, and intellectual property rights such as patents.

A declaration of conflict of interest should include the identity of the person with the conflict of interest, the type of incentive or inducement, and its source.

SELECT the most appropriate option from the suggested_text below:
- Option 1: Investigator receives personal financial payment from an external source
- Option 2: The institution/hospital receives financial payment (indirect conflict)
- Option 3: Sponsor reimburses hospital/researcher for study costs (sponsored studies — most common)
- Option 4: Researchers have a general interest in completing the study (internally funded studies — minimal conflict)
sections.suggested_text:
<for Option 1, personal payment to investigator, use the following>
The {{identify individual, e.g., study doctor/researcher}}, {{insert name}}, is receiving personal financial payment from {{identify source of funds e.g., the study Sponsor}} for {{include reason for payment e.g., providing advice on the design of the study}}. You may request details about this payment.
OR
<for option 2, the institution/hospital receiving financial payment, use the following>
The {{insert recipient of funding e.g., hospital}} is receiving financial payment from the {{Sponsor/Funder}} to cover the cost of conducting this study.
OR
<For option 3, sponsored studies, use the following>
{{Insert name of company}}, the sponsor of this study, will reimburse the hospital and researcher for the costs of doing this study. All of these people have an interest in completing this study. Their interests should not influence your decision to participate in this study.
OR
<For option 4, internally funded studies, use the following>
Researchers have an interest in completing this study. Their interests should not influence your decision to participate in this study.

sections.heading: WHY IS THIS STUDY BEING DONE?
sections.instructions:
OUTPUT STRUCTURE: Your filled_template must contain TWO parts in this exact order:
  1. BACKGROUND (first): 2–3 sentences describing the background and rationale for the study (free-form from the protocol — there is no fixed required/suggested wording for this part).
  2. PURPOSE (second): the required_text sentence beginning exactly with "The purpose of this study is to", with {{explain the purpose of the study}} filled in plain lay language.

BACKGROUND: Begin with 2–3 sentences describing the background and rationale for the study. Include relevant experience or evidence to date, what led to the development of the study (e.g., findings from previous research, unmet needs, gaps in knowledge, or clinical experience), and the current standard of care or existing approaches, if applicable.

PURPOSE: After providing the background context, explain the purpose of the study from the perspective of what a research participant should understand about why the study is being conducted. Focus on why the study is being done and what the researchers hope to learn. Begin the purpose statement with the exact required_text: "The purpose of this study is to...".

Use clear, everyday language that can be easily understood by someone without a medical or research background. Do not describe detailed study procedures or activities.

Writing style — apply to all text generated for this section:
• Plain language: use common everyday words and short sentences. Spell out any abbreviation or acronym on first use.
• Research framing: use correct research terminology (e.g. "investigational study drug," not "treatment" or "therapy"). Do not imply guaranteed outcomes — state explicitly that benefits are uncertain.
• Participant-centred tone: say "you will be asked to" rather than "you will be expected to". Maintain a neutral, non-coercive, non-persuasive tone throughout.
sections.required_text: The purpose of this study is to {{explain the purpose of the study}}

sections.heading: HOW MANY PEOPLE WILL TAKE PART IN THIS STUDY?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions: Indicate the total number of participants, where this study is taking place, and how many participants are specifically particpating at University Health Network (UHN), inclusive of any UHN sites. Indicate how long the study will take overall and when results are expected to be available. Note: Do not discuss the length of individual participation in the study in this section. This section should indicate the total study length. For the research site location, do not specify the actual site name. Use only a general geographical reference (e.g., 'Canada', 'North America', 'around the world').
sections.required_text:
It is anticipated that about {{insert total number of participants, across all sites}} people will take part in this study. {{If research is multi-site, note the locations of other research sites (e.g., Canada/around the world/North America) and the number of participants expected from UHN; if this is a single-site (UHN only) study, omit this sentence}}.

This study should take {{total length of study in months or years}} to complete and the results should be known in about {{anticipated time to complete analysis and have results be available, in months or years}}.

sections.heading: WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?
sections.instructions:
Populate only with activities the participant is asked to do as part of the study after enrollment, and only if explicitly stated in the protocol. Do not include internal naming conventions or codenames used only by the study team (describe procedures in plain language instead), details of the statistical analysis plan, the consent process itself, or how compensation is administered (compensation details belong in the 'Are Study Participants Paid?' section).

If no study related visits are required, indicate this.

If just a few visits are required, indicate the approximate duration of each visit.

If applicable, indicate if and where procedures are to be performed outside of UHN or at varying UHN sites.

Writing style — apply to all text generated for this section:
• Plain language: use common everyday words and short sentences. Spell out any abbreviation or acronym on first use.
• Research framing: use correct research terminology (e.g. "investigational study drug," not "treatment" or "therapy"). Do not imply guaranteed outcomes — state explicitly that benefits are uncertain.
• Participant-centred tone: say "you will be asked to" rather than "you will be expected to". Maintain a neutral, non-coercive, non-persuasive tone throughout.
sections.suggested_text:
<If no study related visits are required, use the following text to indicate this>
No study related visits are required.

<If the patient is required to remain on site after standard of care visits, indicate using the following text as an example>
You will be asked to remain on site after your standard of care visits for approximately 15 minutes for study related activities/We will gather information about you from your medical chart.

<If just a few visits are required, indicate the approximate duration of each visit using the following text as an example>
There will be two (2) study visits during your participation in this study. Visit 1 will be one (1) hour and Visit 2 will be 30 minutes.

<If applicable, indicate if procedures are to be performed outside of UHN or at varying UHN sites, using the following text as an example>
Study Visit 1 will take place at the Toronto Rehabilitation Institute, Lyndhurst Centre and Study Visit 2 will take place at Toronto Western Hospital.

sections.heading: WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?
sections.instructions:
In a bullet format, provide a description of the research procedures and the nature of participation. Ensure that the information provided accurately describes the procedures being used in this specific study. Include a lay explanation, if not obvious, of what each test involves.

For imaging procedures: use the imaging suggested_text example ONLY when imaging is performed for research purposes only (i.e., the scans would not normally be done for this population's medical care / will not be used to guide medical care). Specify the standard clinical imaging procedure, explain the deviation from normal care, and state the number of times imaging will be done. Do not use the imaging example block for imaging that is simply part of routine medical care.

If applicable, list study-related procedures (in bullet format). 

If there are no procedures required of the participants, proceed to the next sections to explain what will happen in the study. Don't include repositories, databases, focus groups, interviews, questionnaires or participant diaries in this section as they belong in a separate section.

Writing style — apply to all text generated for this section:
• Plain language: use common everyday words and short sentences.
• Research framing: use correct research terminology (e.g. "investigational study drug," not "treatment" or "therapy"). Do not imply guaranteed outcomes — state explicitly that benefits are uncertain.
• Participant-centred tone: say "you will be asked to" rather than "you will be expected to". Maintain a neutral, non-coercive, non-persuasive tone throughout.
sections.suggested_text:
<Example for studies involving imaging>
You will be asked to have {{insert name of standard clinical imaging procedure}}.  This scan is already used in medical care, but would not normally be done {{explain deviation from normal care of the study population}}. You will be asked to have this {{enter number of times}} times throughout this study.

<If applicable, list other study-related procedures (in bullet format).Include a lay explaination, if not obvious, of what each test involves. From the following list, list only those that relevant to the study. Example>
The following will be done as part of this study:
• Medical History
• Physical Exam
• ECG (Electrocardiogram)- An electrocardiogram is a test that measures the electrical activity of the heart. Patches attached by wires to a machine will be put on your chest so that the machine can record the pattern of your heart beats.
• Skin Photography - Describe exactly what will be photographed
• Videography - Describe exactly what will be videotaped
• Pulmonary Function Test - A group of tests that measure how well your lungs take in and let out air and how well they move oxygen into your blood.  For this test, you will take deep breaths and blow into a tube connected to a machine.
• Echo (Echocardiogram) – A test that uses sound waves to create a moving picture of the heart to measure how well your heart is functioning.  The picture is much more detailed that a regular x-ray picture and does not involve any radiation exposure.  An instrument that sends high frequency sound waves will be placed on your ribs near the breastbone directed toward your heart.
• X-ray– Specify what part(s) of the body will be scanned
• Dexa Scan - A bone mineral density scan is a special x-ray test that measures the amount of calcium in bones.  It is a non-invasive procedure and it takes about 15 - 30 minutes.
• MUGA Scan - A radioactive tracer is injected via IV (inside your vein) which attaches to blood cells.  Then an instrument is used to see inside your heart.
• MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) - Use of magnetic waves to take pictures of the inside of your body.  You will have to lie still in a MRI machine but will be able to speak to someone at all times.
• MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) with gadolinium contrast - Use of magnetic waves to take pictures of the inside of your body.  You will have to lie still in a MRI machine but will be able to speak to someone at all times.  Prior to the MRI scan you will have a gadolinium contrast injection via IV (inside your vein).

The scans are being done for research purposes only, and will not be used to guide your medical care.

sections.heading: WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?
sections.instructions:
CONDITIONAL: Populate only if the study explicitly describes creating, maintaining, or contributing to a database, registry, or repository. Include only if the protocol explicitly states that data/samples will be entered into a database, registry, biobank, or repository, or describes ongoing storage or potential reuse beyond the current study. Do not populate this section if data/samples are mentioned only as being collected or analyzed for the current study with no database/registry/repository described. Do not describe general data-handling details here — that is covered elsewhere.

When populating: specify the source of information (e.g., medical chart) and the responsible individual/group who will maintain the database. If the database information or samples will be used or shared for future research, include the future-research paragraph.
sections.suggested_text:
<Example for repositories or database studies>
The researchers will collect information about you from {{specify source of information e.g., your medical chart}} and enter this information into an electronic database.  The data will be securely stored, and will be maintained by {{specify responsible individual/group}}.  The database can only be accessed by people who are involved in research.

Please talk to the research team if there is information that you do not feel comfortable sharing.

<If the database information or samples be used or shared for future research, include the following (as applicable)>
Your coded study data and/or coded samples may be used or shared with other researchers (inside and outside of Canada) for future studies.  “Coded” means that directly identifying information (such as your name and date of birth) will be replaced by a number, which will be applied to the study data and/or samples. The code matching your {{study data and/or samples}} with your name and other directly identifying information will be kept by the UHN study team.

This may include storing the {{coded study data and/or samples}} in
• Controlled-access {{databases or biobanks}}.  Access to them is limited to researcher(s) who submit a study plan and who sign an agreement to use the coded study data and/or coded samples only for that research.
• Open access, publicly accessible databases.  Only very limited coded study data may be placed in such databases. The goal of sharing is to make more research possible.

You will not be asked if you agree to take part in future research studies using your {{study data and/or samples}}. You or your study doctor will not be told what type of research will be done. You will not be given reports or other information about any research that is done with your {{study data and/or samples}}.

sections.heading: WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?
sections.instructions: Specify how many focus group(s) and information about timing (e.g., before you begin the study and then every X weeks/months). Specify length in minutes or hours and the location. Explain topics of discussion. Specify if any recording devices will be used.

A focus group is a small group of representative people who are asked to speak about their opinions as part of the research.  A moderator will organize the focus group(s).  Each focus group discussion will be about {{specify length in minutes or hours}} in length and will take place {{specify location}}.  You will be asked to speak about {{explain topics of discussion e.g., your experiences with condition/intervention}}.

While the study team will take precautions to protect your confidentiality, we cannot guarantee that other members of the focus group will respect your privacy or keep the discussions of the group confidential.

During this interview, you will speak with/meet with a member/members of the research team and {{specify others if applicable}}. sections.heading: WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?
sections.instructions: Specify if the interview/focus group will be recorded.
sections.suggested_text: You will be {{audio/video}} recorded during the {{specify e.g., interview(s)/focus group}}. The purpose of the recording is to ensure that the researchers are able to gather complete and accurate information. The recordings will be transcribed and then deleted.

sections.heading: WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?
sections.instructions:
CONDITIONAL: Populate only if the activity is self-completed structured questions (a written or online survey/form completed independently by the participant, without real-time interaction with a researcher). Include this section if it is described as a questionnaire, survey, form, assessment (for example, quality-of-life assessment), screening tool, validated tool, validated instrument (for example, SF-36 or MoCA), or other named assessment completed by the participant on their own. Do not populate this section if the questions are asked during a live interaction (classified as Interview, as it belongs in a different section) or are part of a repeated self-recording over time (classified as Participant Diary, as it belongs in a different section).

Provide information about the timing of questionnaires. Include a description of the purpose. Indicate the estimated time to complete in minutes.

If the questions are of a sensitive nature, explain that they might experience emotional distress, explain what they should do and what type of help will be provided if this happens.

If questionnaires include medically relevant information, but won't be reviewed, note that the responses will not be reviewed by their health care team or study team, and that information should be brought to their attention if they wish for their health care team to know.

Writing style — apply to all text generated for this section:
• Plain language: use common everyday words and short sentences
• Research framing: use correct research terminology (e.g. "investigational study drug," not "treatment" or "therapy"). Do not imply guaranteed outcomes — state explicitly that benefits are uncertain.
• Participant-centred tone: say "you will be asked to" rather than "you will be expected to". Maintain a neutral, non-coercive, non-persuasive tone throughout.
sections.suggested_text:
You will be provided with a questionnaire {{provide information about the timing of questionnaires e.g., before you begin the study and then every two weeks for a year}}. The purpose of the questionnaire is {{include description of purpose e.g., to understand how the study intervention and illness affects your quality of life}}.  Each questionnaire will take about {{indicate estimated time to complete in minutes}} to complete.

The information you provide is for research purposes only.  Some of the questions are personal.  You can choose not to answer questions if you wish.

<If the questions are of a sensitive nature, explain that they might experience emotional distress, explain what should they do and what type of help will be provided if this happens>

<If questionnaires include medically relevant information, but won't be reviewed, include the following>
Even though you may have provided information on a questionnaire, these responses will not be reviewed by your health care team or study team - if you wish them to know this information please bring it to their attention.

With greater application of whole genome/exome sequencing, consideration should be given a priori to the likelihood that inheritable conditions or actionable genetic incidental findings may be discovered during the course of the research. This risk should be reflected in the consenting process. In general, these risks are not applicable to pharmacogenetic testing of specific drugs or drug combinations.

Hereditary genetic testing (to look at whether {{specify condition}} runs in families) {{will not/will/may}} be done on these samples.

<Include if applicable (i.e., sequencing of a human germline or somatic specimen with the intent to generate the genome or exome sequence of that specimen)>
The study {{will/may}} involve whole genome sequencing. Whole genome sequencing is the analysis of the complete set of genetic instructions in a cell.

Every person has their own unique set of genes or “genome”. The reason this is important is because genetic results might contain information (for example, an inherited genetic disease) that could impact you or your biological (blood) relatives.  When you donate your genetic information or materials you are sharing information about yourself, and it can be used to identify these relatives.

Even with protections in place, absolute confidentiality cannot be guaranteed. Advances in technology could also increase the risk that your genetic samples and results could be linked back to you or your relatives.  There is no way to predict what effects such an information loss would have. For example, if an insurer, a current or future employer, or law enforcement were to learn your genetic code it could result in loss of privacy and to possible future discrimination in employment or insurance against you or your relatives.  Even though this risk is unlikely, we think you should be aware. However, the only identifying information that will be present on the sample is your study number.

Due to the rapid pace of technological advances, the potential future use of genetic information is unknown and therefore the potential future risks also are unknown and there may be a risk that the genetic information in the samples could be linked back to you.

You will be {{given the choice/not given the choice}} to find out about genetics testing results.

During the discussions, participants will be encouraged to refrain from using names.  If names or other identifying information is shared during the discussion, it will not be included in the written records.

<<If video/audio recording, describe confidentiality measures including, for example, who will have access, how long they will be kept, and whether they will be sent outside the institution. For example>>
The video/audio recordings will be stored in a secure location and viewed only by members of the research team.  The recordings will be kept until they have been transcribed (turned into written records), and then they will be destroyed.

<<If identifiable data are to be sent outside the institution/study uses a third party to perform study related activities>>
This study requires the transfer of identifiable information to {{insert name of institution/individual}} for the purposes of {{specify purpose}}. The following information will be transferred:
• {{Specify identifiable information to be transferred}}

If the results of this study are published, your identity will remain confidential. It is expected that the information collected during this study will be {{include description of proposed uses of data, e.g., used in analyses and will be published/ presented to the scientific community at meetings and in journals}}.

Even though the likelihood that someone may identify you from the study data is very small, it can never be completely eliminated.

<<If study is a Health Canada regulated study, insert the following>>
The study doctor will keep any personal health information about you in a secure and confidential location for 15 years as required.

<<If study is NOT a Health Canada regulated study, insert the following>>
The study doctor will keep any personal health information about you in a secure and confidential location for 10 years.

Your participation in this study will also be recorded in your medical record at this hospital.

sections.heading: HOW WILL PARTICIPANT INFORMATION BE KEPT CONFIDENTIAL?
sections.sub_section: Research Information in Shared Clinical Records
sections.instructions:
OUTPUT STRUCTURE: Your filled_template must contain the required_text verbatim as the opening paragraph (the UHN hospital records / computer system statement — do not change a word), followed by any applicable suggested_text blocks.

For the suggested_text, resolve each conditional by searching the protocol:
- <<If data or samples are to be sent outside of Canada>>: Include if the protocol specifies data or samples will be transferred to sites outside Canada (e.g., to a central lab, sponsor, or database in the US or Europe).
- <<For studies using smartphones, apps or applicable technology>>: Include if the study uses a mobile app, wearable device, or third-party digital platform to collect study data. Fill in the app/tool/device name from the protocol.
- <<For studies funded or supported by a US federal funding agency where researchers will NOT be using specimens or information for future research>>: Include only for US federally funded studies that will not use samples/data for future research even if de-identified.

If none of the conditions apply, output only the required_text.
sections.required_text: If you participate in this study, information about you from this research project may be stored in your hospital file and in the UHN computer system.  The UHN shares the patient information stored on its computers with other hospitals and health care providers in Ontario so they can access the information if it is needed for your clinical care.  The study team can tell you what information about you will be stored electronically and may be shared outside of the UHN.  If you have any concerns about this, or have any questions, please contact the UHN Privacy Office at 416-340-4800, x6937 (or by email at privacy@uhn.ca).
sections.suggested_text:
<<If data or samples are to be sent outside of Canada>>
Any information {{and/or samples}} sent outside of Canadian borders may increase the risk of disclosure of information because the laws in other countries dealing with protection of information may not be as strict as in Canada. However, all study data {{and/or samples}} that are transferred outside of Canada will be coded. This means they will not contain your personal identifying information such as your name, address, medical health number or contact information.

<<For studies using smartphones, apps or applicable technology to collect the study data, specify the data to be collected and describe the security of the device/application>>
Data collected using the {{insert app/tool/device name}} reside on the {{insert name e.g., Apple}} servers and no assurance can be made about their confidentiality or that they will only be used for research purposes.

<<For studies funded or supported by a US federal funding agency (e.g., NIH, DHHS, etc.) where researchers will NOT be using specimens or information for future research (even if identifiers are removed). This paragraph is not required for non-US federally funded studies>>
Your study data and/or samples will not be used or shared with other researchers for future studies, even if the researchers remove any information that could directly identify you.

sections.heading: WILL FAMILY DOCTORS/HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS KNOW WHO IS PARTICIPATING IN THIS STUDY?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
NOTE: This section is optional for minimal risk studies — include only if relevant to this specific study. It is required for above minimal risk studies.

CHOOSE ONE of the two options in the suggested_text (they are mutually exclusive):
  - Option 1 (default for most therapeutic studies): Family doctor WILL or MAY be informed — use 'will' if it is standard practice to inform the family doctor; use 'may' if there are circumstances where the family doctor would not be informed.
  - Option 2: Family doctor will NOT be informed — use for studies where confidentiality considerations mean the family doctor should not be routinely notified (e.g., some psychiatric, sexual health, or healthy volunteer studies).
sections.suggested_text:
<<Option 1 — Family doctor will or may be informed>>
Your family doctor/health care provider {{will/may}} be informed that you are taking part in a study so that you can be provided with appropriate medical care. If you do not want your family doctor/health care provider to be informed, please discuss this with the study team.

<<Option 2 — Family doctor will NOT be informed>>
OR
Your family doctor/health care provider will not be informed by the study team that you are taking part in the study.  You can choose to let your family doctor/health care provider know, if you like.

sections.heading: WILL INFORMATION ABOUT THIS STUDY BE AVAILABLE?
complexity: Easy - Standard text, no mapping required
sections.required_text: Study results will be shared with you if/when they become available after the entire study is completed. It is expected that this may take a number of years. The results will be shared with you based on your preferred communication method indicated in UHN's medical record system. Please talk to your study doctor if you have any questions about the results.

sections.heading: WHAT IS THE COST TO PARTICIPANTS?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
If participation could result in additional costs, include an explanation of these potential costs. Ensure that examples of extra costs are consistent with the research project.

If participation will not result in any costs, include the no-additional-costs statement.
sections.suggested_text:
<<If participation could result in additional costs, include an explanation of these potential costs. For example>>
Taking part in this study may result in added costs to you.  For example:
• There may be costs associated with study visits.  For example, parking or transportation, or snacks/meals during your stay.
• You may miss work as a result of participation in this study.

<<OR If participation will not result in any costs, include the following>>
Participation in this study will not involve any additional costs to you or your private health care insurance.

sections.heading: ARE STUDY PARTICIPANTS PAID TO BE IN THIS STUDY?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
Describe compensation provided to participants, or state if no compensation is provided.

If receipts or other documentation is required for re-imbursement, this must be justified to the REB and must be described.
sections.suggested_text:
<<If there is no payment for participation>>
You will not be paid for taking part in this study.

<<OR If participants are receiving any token of appreciation (revise as applicable to the study)>>
If you decide to participate in this study, you will receive ${{specify amount}} and, if applicable, {{specify the interval e.g., every three months}}.

<<If there is re-imbursement of costs for participation>>
If you decide to participate in this study, you will be reimbursed ${{enter actual or maximum dollar amount}} for some study related expenses such as {{list reimbursable expenses as applicable}}.

<<If receipts or other documentation is required for re-imbursement, this must be justified to the REB and must be described. For example>>
You will need to provide your receipts for {{insert expense types e.g., parking}} to the research staff in order to be reimbursed.

sections.heading: WHAT WILL HAPPEN IF PARTICIPANT IS INJURED DURING THE STUDY?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
NOTE: This section is optional for minimal risk studies — include only if relevant to this specific study. It is required for above minimal risk studies.

Describe next steps in case of research-related injury.

This section shall not have qualifiers that suggest that a patient's rights to care could potentially be compromised in the event of study related injury and should only include the standard UHN wording.

Examples of Unacceptable Wording:
• “If you are treated according to the protocol, you will be covered by insurance held by the sponsor for medical costs arising from any study-related injury.”
• “If you suffer any side effect or other physical injury resulting directly from the study drug, the Sponsor will pay for the reasonable costs of medical treatment to the extent permitted by the law of your country if: (a) You took the study drug as directed by the Study Doctor and your injury was not deliberately caused; (b) The Study Doctor was immediately notified about your injury, and the medical advice of the Study Doctor was followed.”
sections.suggested_text: In the case of research-related side effects or injury, medical care will be provided by {{specify e.g., your doctor or you will be referred for appropriate medical care}}.

sections.heading: COMMERCIALISATION
sections.instructions:
NOTE: This section is optional for minimal risk studies — include only if relevant to this specific study. It is required for above minimal risk studies.

CONDITIONAL: Include this section only if the research could lead to commercial products (e.g., new drugs, devices, diagnostic tests). Alter as needed to fit the research.

Determine from the protocol or study context whether commercial development is a possibility. If yes, choose the appropriate sub-option:
  - Option 1: Participants will NOT receive a share of any commercial profit (most common)
  - Option 2: Participants WILL receive a share of commercial profits (rare — specify details)

If there is no possibility of commercialization, omit this section.
sections.suggested_text:
<<If applicable (alter as needed to fit the research)>>
It is possible that the research conducted using your samples and/or study data may eventually lead to the development of new diagnostic tests, new drugs or devices, or other commercial products.

<<If participants will not share in commercial profit>>
There are no plans to provide payment to you if this happens.

<<If participants will share in commercial profits>>
If this happens, you will receive {{describe the participant's share in commercial profit}}.

sections.heading: WHAT ARE THE RIGHTS OF PARTICIPANTS IN A RESEARCH STUDY?
complexity: Easy - Standard text, no mapping required
sections.required_text:
You will be told, in a timely manner, about new information that may be relevant to your willingness to stay in this study.

Your rights to privacy are legally protected by federal and provincial laws that require safeguards to ensure that your privacy is respected.

By signing this form you do not give up any of your legal rights against the study doctor, sponsor or involved institutions for compensation, nor does this form relieve the study doctor, sponsor or their agents of their legal and professional responsibilities.

sections.heading: WHAT IF RESEARCHERS DISCOVER SOMETHING ABOUT A RESEARCH PARTICIPANT?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
NOTE: This section is optional — include only if the protocol explicitly anticipates or addresses incidental findings. If the protocol does not mention incidental findings or a plan for disclosing unexpected results, omit this section entirely.

If incidental findings are anticipated as a result of the study, include this section and address what information will be provided to participants. Indicate the anticipated incidental findings and the anticipated management plan.
sections.suggested_text:
During the study, the researchers may learn something about you that they didn't expect.  For example, the researchers may {{insert anticipated incidental findings e.g. find out that you have another medical condition}}.

<<Describe anticipated management plan. Examples — choose ONE>>
If any new clinically important information about your health is obtained as a result of your participation in this study, you will be informed.
or
If any new information relevant to your or your relatives' health is obtained as a result of your participation in this study, you will be given the opportunity to decide whether you wish to be made aware of that information.

sections.heading: WHOM DO PARTICIPANTS CONTACT FOR QUESTIONS?
complexity: Not in protocol - requires manual entry
sections.instructions:
Fill in the {{insert person's name and telephone}} placeholders in the required_text with the Principal Investigator's (or designated study contact's) name and telephone number.

The REB contact details (UHN REB Chair, 416-581-7849) are standard and must not be modified.

sections.required_text:
If you have questions about taking part in this study, or if you suffer a research-related injury, you can talk to the research team, or the person who is in charge of the study at this institution. That person is:

____________________________     _________________________
Name                                                       Telephone
